title: Information Compression at Criticality
authors: Simon Jiricek, Miroslav Hopjan, Boris Altshuler, Vladimir Kravtsov, Lev Vidmar
abstract: Highly excited quantum states at the critical boundary of ergodicity are known to deviate from thermal behavior, yet their dynamical properties remain poorly understood. Here, we uncover the complexity of quantum dynamics at criticality through the lens of intrinsic information compression in energy space. We show that the Hamiltonian spectrum can be systematically truncated, yielding a simplified description of the dynamics while preserving its essential features. Specifically, for both interacting and noninteracting systems, we demonstrate that a vanishing fraction of Hamiltonian eigenlevels suffices to reproduce the power-law decay of the survival probability. The resulting truncated spectrum exhibits a fractal structure characterized by a level-spacing distribution with a power-law tail, while its spectral form factor displays the same asymptotic power-law decay as the survival probability.
summary: The paper develops a method based on intrinsic information compression to study quantum dynamics at criticality in various disordered models. By truncating the Hamiltonian spectrum to only essential energy levels, the authors show that the resulting simplified description accurately predicts key dynamical observables like the survival probability decay. This establishes energy-space compression as a fundamental principle governing critical behavior.
main_problem: The study aims to understand quantum dynamics at the critical boundary of ergodicity, where highly excited states deviate from thermal behavior, by finding efficient ways to describe their complex energy space.
main_result: The power-law decay of the survival probability at criticality can be accurately reproduced using only a vanishing fraction of the total Hamiltonian eigenlevels, establishing intrinsic information compression in energy space.
method: The core method involves an intrinsic information compression technique applied to the energy spectrum, where dynamics are approximated by truncating the Hamiltonian basis to include only the most significant eigenstates.
model_or_system: The research investigates various quantum many-body systems exhibiting ergodicity breaking transitions, including the 3D Anderson model (3DA), Power-law Random Banded Model (PLRB), Quantum Sun Model (QSM), and Ultrametric Model (UM).
key_observables: Survival Probability $R(	au)$, Spectral Form Factor (SFF) $	ilde{K}(	au)$, Wavefunction Fractal Dimension ($d_2$), and the level-spacing distribution exponent ($\Delta_2$).
important_parameters: The critical exponents, such as $d'_2$ and $	ilde{\delta}_2$, are key; the analysis focuses on the thermodynamic limit where the fraction of retained levels vanishes.
main_assumptions: It is assumed that the dynamics can be effectively captured by a small subset of energy eigenstates (intrinsic information compression), and localized states at spectral edges must be filtered out to reveal true critical behavior.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the agreement between $R(	au)$ and $	ilde{K}(	au)$ via power-law decay, show the fractal nature ($	ilde{\delta}_2 < 1$) of the truncated spectrum, and map out gap ratios distinguishing localized, delocalized, and critical states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes multiple disordered models (3DA, PLRB, QSM, UM) by first identifying spectral edges containing localized states. It then applies energy-space truncation to filter these edges, demonstrating that the resulting truncated Spectral Form Factor accurately mimics the power-law decay of the survival probability at criticality.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool—energy-space compression—to analyze complex quantum dynamics near critical points in disordered systems, offering insights applicable to many condensed matter problems where full diagonalization is impossible.
